correctness.rationale: Convolution idempotent m*chi_r and normalized Weyl integration give 2m/pi times I_m=integral_0^pi |sin(m theta)|sin theta dtheta. Split at j*pi/m, use the explicit sine-antiderivative, and sum sin(j*pi/m)=cot(pi/(2m)) to prove I_m=2m/(m²−1)cot(pi/(2m)). Endpoint Linfty sign and L1 approximate-identity arguments are valid for integrable kernels. Direct independent high-precision piecewise quadrature for sample m and finite source checker structure corroborate the exact algebra; m=1 treated separately. No false finite-to-infinite extrapolation.
